title: Multi-Disciplinary Case Review
subtitle: How CrisPRO supports your tumor board with drug ranking, resistance forecasting, and evidence assembly

case_context.cancer: High-grade serous ovarian cancer, Stage IVB
case_context.situation: Post 4 cycles carboplatin + bevacizumab. Disease is advanced with peritoneal carcinomatosis, pleural effusions, and lymph node involvement.
case_context.key_question: What treatment options remain, and which best match this patient's tumor biology?
case_context.data_completeness: 55% — has IHC and germline, missing NGS, BRCA/HRD, CA-125 series

stages.name: Case Overview
stages.plain_language: The tumor board view starts with a complete case summary: patient demographics, diagnosis, staging, treatment history, biomarker results, and imaging findings. Everything the board needs is on one screen, sourced directly from the patient's medical reports.

patient_summary.prior_treatment: Carboplatin + Bevacizumab x4 cycles (completed Jan 2026, bevacizumab held cycle 4 due to proteinuria)
patient_summary.disease_burden: Peritoneal carcinomatosis, ascites, bilateral pleural effusions, abdominopelvic lymphadenopathy
patient_summary.germline: MBD4 homozygous pathogenic (c.1293delA, p.K431Nfs*54), PDGFRA VUS (p.S755P)

stages.name: Data Readiness Assessment
stages.plain_language: Before recommending treatments, CrisPRO assesses how complete the patient's data is. A 55% completeness score means we have enough to make baseline recommendations, but critical tests are missing. Each missing test is flagged with what it would unlock — for example, BRCA/HRD testing unlocks Level 2 analysis, which adds synthetic lethality detection and more precise drug ranking.

data_shown.confidence_cap: Level 1 recommendations only — higher confidence requires additional testing

missing_tests.unlocks: Level 2 analysis — PARP inhibitor eligibility, synthetic lethality detection
missing_tests.clinical_impact: Determines whether PARP inhibitors (olaparib, niraparib) are an option. ~50% of HGS ovarian cancers have HRD.

missing_tests.unlocks: Level 2 analysis — HRD-positive classification expands PARP inhibitor eligibility beyond BRCA
missing_tests.clinical_impact: HRD-positive patients benefit from PARP inhibitors even without BRCA mutation

missing_tests.unlocks: Level 2 analysis — somatic mutation profile, TMB, actionable alterations
missing_tests.clinical_impact: Identifies additional targeted therapy options and clinical trial eligibility

missing_tests.unlocks: Level 3 analysis — treatment response monitoring, recurrence detection
missing_tests.clinical_impact: Enables longitudinal response tracking and early recurrence detection

missing_tests.unlocks: Level 3 analysis — CCNE1 amplification, BRCA reversion detection
missing_tests.clinical_impact: CCNE1 amplification predicts PARP inhibitor resistance; BRCA reversion confirms acquired resistance

data_shown.recommendation: Order BRCA/HRD testing and tumor NGS panel before next tumor board. These two tests unlock the highest-value analysis levels.

stages.name: Drug Ranking
stages.plain_language: CrisPRO ranks available treatments by how well each drug's mechanism matches this patient's tumor biology. The ranking considers what pathways the drug targets, what resistance mechanisms the tumor has, and what biomarkers predict response. Each drug gets a fit score from 0 to 1, with the reasoning shown for why it scored high or low.

data_shown.how_it_works: Each drug is profiled by its mechanism of action (what biological pathways it targets). The patient's tumor is profiled by which pathways are active. Drugs that target active pathways in this tumor score higher. The score combines eligibility (can the patient receive this drug?) with mechanism fit (does the drug target the right pathways?).

drugs.name: Olaparib (PARP inhibitor)
drugs.fit_rationale: Targets DNA repair deficiency. If BRCA/HRD is positive, this is the strongest match. MBD4 mutation may enhance sensitivity through impaired DNA repair.

drugs.name: Niraparib (PARP inhibitor)
drugs.fit_rationale: Same mechanism class as olaparib. Broader HRD-positive eligibility. Also used as maintenance therapy.

drugs.name: Pembrolizumab + chemotherapy combination
drugs.fit_rationale: PD-L1 positive (CPS 10) provides rationale for checkpoint inhibitor. MSS status limits single-agent efficacy, but combination with chemotherapy may overcome this.
drugs.blocking_factor: MSS status reduces likelihood of response

drugs.name: Doxorubicin (liposomal)
drugs.fit_rationale: Standard option for platinum-resistant ovarian cancer. Different mechanism from prior carboplatin, reducing cross-resistance.
drugs.blocking_factor: No specific biomarker match — empirical choice

drugs.name: Mirvetuximab soravtansine (ELAHERE)
drugs.fit_rationale: FR-alpha targeted antibody-drug conjugate. Requires FR-alpha >= 75% positivity.

data_shown.ranking_note: Current ranking is at Level 1 (baseline). Adding BRCA/HRD and NGS data will refine the ranking and may promote PARP inhibitors to confirmed strong matches.

stages.name: Resistance Forecast
stages.plain_language: For each recommended treatment, CrisPRO forecasts the most likely resistance mechanisms — how the tumor might adapt to survive. This lets the board plan ahead: which drug to try first, what to switch to when resistance develops, and whether combination therapy could block multiple escape routes simultaneously.

resistance_mechanisms.biology: Tumor restores BRCA function through secondary mutations, repairing DNA damage and escaping PARP inhibitor effect.
resistance_mechanisms.monitoring: Serial ctDNA testing can detect BRCA reversion before clinical progression
resistance_mechanisms.backup_strategy: Switch to non-PARP mechanism (immunotherapy combination, chemotherapy)

resistance_mechanisms.biology: CCNE1 amplification activates alternative cell cycle pathways that bypass the DNA repair vulnerability.
resistance_mechanisms.monitoring: RNA expression testing (Level 3) can detect CCNE1 amplification
resistance_mechanisms.backup_strategy: CDK2 inhibitors (clinical trial), or switch mechanism class

resistance_mechanisms.biology: Tumor increases production of proteins that pump the drug out of cells.
resistance_mechanisms.backup_strategy: Dose adjustment or combination with efflux inhibitor

forecasts.strategic_implication: If PARP inhibitors are used, plan for BRCA reversion monitoring via ctDNA. Have a backup plan ready before resistance develops.

resistance_mechanisms.biology: In MSS tumors, the immune microenvironment suppresses T-cell activity over time, even with checkpoint blockade.
resistance_mechanisms.monitoring: PD-L1 re-testing on progression, TIL assessment
resistance_mechanisms.backup_strategy: Add VEGF inhibitor (bevacizumab) to reprogram microenvironment, or switch to therapeutic vaccine approach

resistance_mechanisms.biology: Tumor stops presenting the antigens that T-cells were targeting.
resistance_mechanisms.backup_strategy: Multi-antigen approaches (therapeutic vaccines presenting multiple targets)

forecasts.strategic_implication: MSS status is the primary barrier. Combination strategies that address the immunosuppressive microenvironment are more likely to succeed than single-agent approaches.

stages.name: Synthetic Lethality Analysis
stages.plain_language: CrisPRO looks for synthetic lethal relationships — pairs where a mutation in the patient's tumor creates a vulnerability that a specific drug can exploit. For example, if a tumor has lost a DNA repair gene, a drug that blocks a backup repair pathway can be lethal to the tumor while sparing normal cells. This analysis runs at Level 2 and requires NGS data.

data_shown.how_it_works: CrisPRO checks the patient's mutation profile against a database of known synthetic lethal pairs. When a tumor loses gene A, and a drug blocks gene B (where A and B are backup systems for each other), the tumor cannot survive — but normal cells still have gene A, so they are spared.
data_shown.current_status: Level 2 analysis not yet available — requires NGS and BRCA/HRD testing

potential_pairs.potential_vulnerability: Impaired DNA repair may create sensitivity to DNA-damaging agents and PARP inhibitors
potential_pairs.evidence_level: Mechanistic hypothesis — MBD4's role in DNA repair is established, but clinical synthetic lethality data is limited
potential_pairs.requires: BRCA/HRD testing to confirm the full DNA repair deficiency profile

potential_pairs.potential_vulnerability: Cell cycle checkpoint deficiency may increase sensitivity to cell cycle inhibitors
potential_pairs.evidence_level: Established — TP53-mutant tumors are known to be sensitive to WEE1/ATR inhibition
potential_pairs.requires: NGS to confirm TP53 mutation type and check for co-mutations

data_shown.what_unlocks_it: Ordering NGS and BRCA/HRD testing will activate Level 2 analysis, including full synthetic lethality detection across all known pairs.

stages.name: Evidence Assembly
stages.plain_language: CrisPRO assembles the evidence behind each recommendation into a structured evidence vault. For every drug ranking, resistance forecast, and synthetic lethality call, the supporting data is traceable — which biomarker, which publication, which clinical trial supports this recommendation. This makes it easy to defend decisions at tumor board and to document the rationale in the medical record.

what_it_contains.items: For each ranked drug: the biomarkers that support it, the mechanism match score, and the source of the biomarker data (which lab, which report)
For each forecasted resistance mechanism: the published literature supporting it, the likelihood estimate, and the monitoring strategy
For each synthetic lethal pair: the published research establishing the relationship, the evidence grade, and the clinical trial status of the targeting drug
A structured table showing which recommendations are confirmed by testing, which are pending test results, and which are mechanistic hypotheses

data_shown.traceability: Every recommendation links back to the specific biomarker result, medical report, or publication that supports it. No recommendation appears without a traceable evidence source.
data_shown.export_options: Evidence vault can be exported as a formatted report for the medical record or as a presentation slide for tumor board

stages.name: Strategic Priorities
stages.plain_language: The tumor board view ends with a prioritized action list. The top priority is defense — understanding and planning for resistance. The second priority is attack — identifying the best treatment targets. The third priority is data — ordering the tests that will unlock deeper analysis. This gives the board a clear, actionable summary.

actions: If PARP inhibitors are used, plan BRCA reversion monitoring via serial ctDNA
Prepare backup treatment plan for when resistance develops
Consider combination therapy to block multiple resistance pathways simultaneously
PARP inhibitors are the strongest potential match — pending BRCA/HRD results
Checkpoint inhibitor + chemotherapy is a moderate match given PD-L1 positivity and MSS status
FR-alpha targeted therapy (ELAHERE) is NOT an option — FR-alpha negative
Discuss clinical trial options for MBD4-mutated tumors and TP53-targeted therapies
Order BRCA1/2 germline and somatic testing — CRITICAL
Order HRD score (Myriad MyChoice or equivalent) — CRITICAL
Order tumor NGS panel — HIGH priority
Establish CA-125 baseline and begin serial monitoring — MODERATE priority
Consider RNA expression testing for CCNE1 and BRCA reversion — MODERATE priority

data_shown.bottom_line: This patient's most promising path is PARP inhibitor therapy, contingent on BRCA/HRD testing. The MBD4 mutation may enhance sensitivity. Without these test results, treatment selection is operating at 55% data completeness — ordering these tests is the single highest-value action.

roadmap_items.description: CrisPRO currently ranks treatments by mechanism fit — how well a drug's targets match the tumor's biology. The ability to predict whether a specific patient will respond to a specific treatment, with quantified confidence, is in development.
roadmap_items.note: Mechanism-fit ranking is available now. Individual response prediction is an active research area.

roadmap_items.description: Level 3 analysis adds longitudinal response tracking (CA-125 trends) and expression-based resistance detection (CCNE1, BRCA reversion). This requires serial CA-125 data and RNA expression testing.
roadmap_items.note: Level 1 and Level 2 analysis are available. Level 3 requires additional data inputs.

roadmap_items.description: Automatic generation of a formatted slide deck for tumor board presentation, including case summary, drug ranking, resistance forecast, and evidence references.
roadmap_items.note: Evidence vault export is available. Full slide deck generation is planned.

roadmap_items.description: Comparison of this patient's biomarker profile and treatment outcomes against similar patients in the CrisPRO database, to identify patterns and inform treatment selection.
roadmap_items.note: Individual patient analysis is available. Cross-patient benchmarking is planned.

governance_labels.validated: Available now, supported by patient data and published evidence
governance_labels.in_development: Active area of development; not yet available for clinical use
governance_labels.mechanistic_hypothesis: Based on biological understanding and published research; requires clinical validation for this specific context
